molecular_glues.abstract: Computer Science > Computational Complexity arXiv:2611.16412 (cs) [Submitted on 12 Nov 2026] Title: Exact Quantum Algorithms for Composed Boolean Functions Authors: Gagan Chiruvella , Chandrima Kayal , Rajat Mittal , Manaswi Paraashar , Nitin Saurabh View a PDF of the paper titled Exact Quantum Algorithms for Composed Boolean Functions, by Gagan Chiruvella and 4 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: We study exact quantum algorithms for block compositions of total Boolean functions. For an outer function $f$ of degree $D$ and an inner function $g$ on $m$ bits, we prove $$ Q_E(f\circ g)=O\!\left(mD+Q_E(f)Q_{1/(4D)}(g)\right). $$ The algorithm combines approximate inner evaluations with a finite exact correction. Its two costs are governed by different parameters of the outer function: exact query complexity determines the cost of simulation, whereas polynomial degree determines the number of inner blocks used in the correction. We first establish the construction with an arity-dependent error threshold and then obtain the degree-dependent threshold above. For recursive ternary not-all-equal, this gives an exact algorithm using $(3/\sqrt2)^{k(1+o(1))}$ queries asymptotically. More generally, for every fixed nonconstant total gadget $h$, we determine the exact recursive rate as $\max\{\textrm{deg}(h),\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(h)\}$ and prove $Q_E(h^{\circ k})=\widetilde O_h(R(h^{\circ k})^2)$. The composition limit also allows to transfer separations from $Q_{\varepsilon}$ and $°$ to exact quantum query complexity $Q_E$ (similar to fractional block sensitivity to block sensitivity transfer in Tal and Kulkarni 2016, Chicago Journal of Theoretical Computer Science). We construct a family with $s=\operatorname{bs}=\operatorname{fbs}\ge Q_E^{3/2-o(1)}$, improving the previous exponent $1.1527\ldots$. A second construction gives $R \ge Q_E^{2-o(1)}$, improving the previous exponent $3/2$. We also allow different inner functions and give analogous quantitative separations in quantum communication. Abstract The minimal number of inputs in the local function of a non-trivial cellular automaton is two. Such a function can be viewed as as a kind of binary operation. If this operation is associative, it forms, together with the set of states, a semigroup. There are 18 semigroups of order 3 up to equivalence, and they define 18 cellular automata rules with three states. We investigate these rules with respect to solvability and show that all of them are solvable, meaning that the state of a given cell after n iterations can be expressed by an explicit formula. We derive the relevant formulae for all 18 rules using some additional properties possessed by particular semigroups of order 3, such as commutativity and idempotence.
